The span [dst, dst + 4*N) grows with the program length N and is never checked against the loader kernel's own in-box ABI words: GH9_EXIT_WORD=703, GH9_TICKS_COUNT=732, GH9_ARGV_WORD=750..752 (argc/argv/envp), GH9_ARGV_RESULT=754, argv data 760..766 (baker.py:2016-2033). Because the window sits at rows 12-24 of a 32-word-wide image, its RAM span overlaps those words by construction.

why_this_matters_for_BK11: The parked note attributed BK-1 leg 2's red (with the DEFECT-16c patch) to the tick handler clobbering live s9/s10/s11. That is refuted as the operative cause: an engine-side prototype of option (a) — snapshot the USER regfile at tick delivery, restore it when the handler returns to the interrupted PC — ran leg 2 with 7/7 ticks made fully transparent (output/opta_treat_bk1.txt) and the gate was STILL red with the same 0x00000000. The corruption happens at step 3084, 448 steps BEFORE the first tick (step 3532), and its value is a program code-pixel word: it is the loader's patch copy, not the tick path.

fix_candidates.1_window_relayout: place the patch window so its RAM span cannot reach the ABI words (e.g. window starting at row 9 -> span [288,672) for 96 instructions), plus a bake-time assertion. No syscall/ABI change, but it moves every GH-9/GH-23/BK-1 gate's window geometry -> needs an arc run.
fix_candidates.2_bounded_copy: make the loader's copy bounded and LOUD: if dst + 4*N would overlap the ABI words, fault/report instead of silently patching over argv. Defensive, no ABI change, makes the class of failure unfailable-silently.
fix_candidates.3_smaller_lbu_lowering: keep the DEFECT-16c fix but shrink the LBU/LHU sequence so the leg-2 program stays <= 88 instructions (HEAD is 84, the held patch makes it 96; 4*88 = 352 -> span [396,748) still misses argv@750).
fix_candidates.4_relocate_abi_words: move GH9_ARGV_*/GH9_TICKS_COUNT out of the window's reach -> an ABI change, i.e. the actual design decision (Jericho's call).
